newsitem.title: USA: Five grilled in FBI van theft; agents hunt weapons.
newsitem.headline: Five grilled in FBI van theft; agents hunt weapons.

text.p: Police said on Thursday they were questioning five people who may have information about the theft of an FBI van full of weapons but no charges had been filed and most of the weapons were still missing.
"No one has been charged yet," a spokeswoman for the Memphis police department said.

The five being questioned were not believed to be the van thieves but may have some information about who did steal the vehicle, the Memphis Commercial Appeal newspaper reported. Three of them were picked up Wednesday in the neighbourhood where the burned-out van was found earlier in the week. Two others were already under arrest in another matter.

Police did recover tear gas canisters and grenade launcher cartridges in the arrests but about a dozen weapons including assault rifles, submachineguns and 8,000 rounds of ammunition were still missing.

The van was stolen from the parking lot of a hotel where a visiting team of FBI agents from Little Rock, Arkansas, spent Monday night. Its burned-out shell was found early on Tuesday on the northern edge of Memphis.

The van had been left unattended in the parking lot with no special locks on the weapons and no burglar alarm. The Little Rock agents were in Memphis for a training exercise for about half a dozen special weapons and tactics squads.

In Washington, Attorney General Janet Reno expressed concern Thursday that the van had been stolen. "I'm troubled when an FBI van is stolen and weapons are taken and the FBI van is destroyed. That's troubling," she said at her weekly Justice Department news conference.

"The FBI is reviewing all the processes and procedures that were in place to see what must be done to address this problem," she said. "We're reviewing it to see what happened, to see if we need to impose new procedures or to take other action."
FBI Director Louis Freeh told a congressional hearing Wednesday that the agency had mounted a "full-court press" in the case because it involved "very dangerous weapons."
